newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian king demurs on fate of exiled prince.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian king demurs on fate of exiled prince.

text.p: Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk said on Tuesday that without the approval of the nation's co-premiers he would not pardon exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh, whose fate has become a political lightning rod.

"In spite of the affection I have for my half-brother (Sirivudh)...I have said officially that no amnesty would be granted by me without the joint agreement of the two prime ministers, Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen," the king stated in a interview with his cabinet released late on Tuesday.

"I would not grant any amnesty to anyone that Hun Sen does not pardon, because it would not be good for Cambodia if the king and one of his prime ministers were to become two enemies," the statement read.
The statement appears to shift the fate of Sirivudh, sentenced for an alleged plot to assassinate Hun Sen, back to the co-premier.
On Monday Hun Sen had said he would welcome Sirivudh's return if the prince were granted a royal pardon.

That statement was a softening of his previous stance on the Sirivudh case. At the weekend, Hun Sen had threatened to call out troops and tanks to prevent Sirivudh's return and implied royal amnesty for Sirivudh would create lawlessness in Cambodia.

Sirivudh was exiled to France nearly one year ago after being accused of plotting to assassinate Hun Sen. He was sentenced to 10 years in jail in absentia. International observers branded the trial a travesty.
Sirivudh has since vowed to return, raising the ire of Hun Sen and fuelling tensions between the co-premiers, who formed an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
Ranariddh has said he supports the return of Sirivudh.
Despite the political turmoil, Sirivudh has said he will not change his plans to return to Cambodia, though he would not reveal the date of his return.
